INLB 201.title: Special Topics in Indigenous Land-based Studies
INLB 201.description: Topics and location will vary from year to year. Experiential, intensive land-based course designed and delivered in collaboration with academic faculty and Indigenous community partner(s).

INLB 210.title: Land and Indigenous Self-Determination: Introduction to Theoretical Perspectives
INLB 210.description: Cultural, political, and economic context that informs the experiences of Indigenous people and communities. Experiential, intensive land-based course designed and delivered in collaboration with academic faculty and Indigenous community partner(s).

INLB 220.title: Land and Indigenous Self-Determination: Introduction to Methods and Application
INLB 220.description: Applied cultural, political, and economic land-based practices that inform and advance Indigenous self-determination. Experiential, intensive land-based course designed and delivered in collaboration with academic faculty and Indigenous community partner(s).

INLB 250.title: Indigenous Knowledge, Science, and Environmental Justice
INLB 250.description: Indigenous ecological knowledge, its intersections with western scientific knowledge, and approaches to environmental justice. Experiential, intensive land-based course designed and delivered in collaboration with academic faculty and Indigenous community partner(s).

INLB 251.title: Introduction to Indigenous Health, Wellness, and Self-Determination
INLB 251.description: Introduction to the social, political, cultural, and gendered determinants of Indigenous Peoples' health and wellness. Experiential, intensive land-based course designed and delivered in collaboration with academic faculty and Indigenous community partner(s).

INLB 252.title: Introduction to Gender Justice and Indigenous Communities
INLB 252.description: Introduction to the politics of gender and sexuality from Indigenous perspectives, with a focus on intersectionality. Experiential, intensive land-based course designed and delivered in collaboration with academic faculty and Indigenous community partner(s).

INLB 310.title: Land and Indigenous Self-Determination: Advanced Theoretical Perspectives
INLB 310.description: Theorizing land and self-determination from Indigenous cultural, political, and economic perspectives. Experiential, intensive land-based course designed and delivered in collaboration with academic faculty and Indigenous community partner(s).

INLB 320.title: Land and Indigenous Self-Determination: Advanced Methods and Application
INLB 320.description: Advanced cultural, political, and economic land-based practices that guide decolonization and Indigenous self-determination. Experiential, intensive land-based course designed and delivered in collaboration with academic faculty and Indigenous community partner(s).

INLB 401.title: Advanced Special Topics in Indigenous Land-Based Studies
INLB 401.description: Topics and location will vary from year to year. Advanced experiential, intensive land-based course designed and delivered in collaboration with academic faculty and Indigenous community partner(s). For further information please consult the departmental website.

INLB 450.title: Decolonizing Science and the Politics of Sustainability
INLB 450.description: Decolonizing ecological knowledge, environmental justice, and the discourse of sustainability. Experiential, intensive land-based course designed and delivered in collaboration with academic faculty and Indigenous community partner(s).

INLB 451.title: Decolonizing Indigenous Health and Wellness
INLB 451.description: The colonial determinants of Indigenous Peoples' health and wellness. The governance of land in relation to health. Experiential, intensive land-based course designed and delivered in collaboration with academic faculty and Indigenous community partner(s).

INLB 452.title: Gender Justice and Indigenous Resurgence
INLB 452.description: The theory and politics of gender and sexuality from Indigenous perspectives. Emphasis on decolonial and intersectional Indigenous feminisms and queer/two-spirit theory. Experiential, intensive land-based course designed and delivered in collaboration with academic faculty and Indigenous community partner(s). Students are eligible for Pass/Fail or percentage grading.
